views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the newly imposed List 3 posture (10% on ~$200B, scheduled to rise to 25% on 1 January 2019) and reopen talks aimed at structural IP/tech-transfer remedies, not another purchase-only truce. Do not launch List 4 now, and do not roll back tariffs or trade purchases for a May-style pause. Use the January rate-hike clock as leverage while offering China a face-saving path back to the table on the Section 301 findings.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a modest US opportunity, not a high-cost emergency. The dispute has reached peak conventional US tariff coverage (~$250B after List 3 took effect 24 September) while China could only answer with 5–10% on ~$60B—it has exhausted dollar-for-dollar tariff space (timeline 2018-09-17/18/24; USTR 18 September; DW/Business Insider). US macro still favors staying power: Michigan sentiment 100.1, industrial production 104.1, VIX 12.89, no recession signal (country_health). China is the more strained party—IP slowing to 105.8, CNY down ~9.5% to 6.88, reserves off ~1.2%—and that yuan move already offsets much of the new 10% duty, which is why a further immediate tariff blast would buy less pressure than it costs. The costs that do exist are concentrated, not systemic: EXPCH is down ~7% and China has targeted soy/pork/farm-belt goods; USDA is already paying the first $4.7B of a $12B aid package, and farm-state Republicans want markets not a bailout. Front-loaded IMPCH (+31% Apr–Sep) and a wider goods deficit show importers racing the tariffs, not a structural US collapse. Action should therefore stay near zero: the May 19 purchase joint statement collapsed within ten days when 301 actions resumed (timeline 2018-05-19/29), so conceding purchases again would repeat a failed bargain. Escalating to the threatened ~$267B List 4 right after China’s expected $60B reply would hit remaining consumer goods into the midterms and could kill the Mnuchin/Kudlow talk channel that was still open in mid-September. Negotiate without new US commitments; keep January 25% and List 4 as contingent pressure, not as the next move this week.
key_factors: List 3 ($200B at 10%, rising to 25% on 1 Jan 2019) just took effect 24 September; combined 301 coverage ~$250B
China's matching tariff capacity is exhausted (~$60B at 5–10%); US still has a contingent List 4 (~$267B)
US real economy still strong (sentiment 100.1, IP up, VIX ~13); China IP slowing and CNY −9.5% offsets the 10% duty
Concentrated US cost is farm-belt retaliation (soybeans, pork) plus $12B USDA aid—political, not systemic GDP damage
May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed in 10 days; talks should target Section 301 structural practices, not another pause

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump directs USTR to finalize List 3: 10% tariffs on ~$200B of Chinese imports effective Sept 24, scheduled to rise to 25% on Jan 1, 2019.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports.
University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment latest 100.1 (2018-09-01), up from 96.2 in August — no demand-collapse signal.
VIX 12.89 on 2018-09-26, down ~45% over the window — markets are not pricing a US crisis.
US goods imports from China rose from $38.2B (Apr) to $49.9B (Sep), +30.6% — front-loading ahead of List 3.
US goods exports to China fell from $10.5B (Apr) to $9.7B (Sep), -7.4% — retaliation is biting ag/export channels.
CNY/USD 6.8763 on 2018-09-26 vs 6.2785 on 2018-04-02, +9.5% — yuan depreciation largely offsets the new 10% List 3 rate.
China industrial production index eased from 107.0 (Apr) to 105.8 (Sep) — growth cooling on the Chinese side.
USTR: List 3 effective 24 Sept at 10%, rising to 25% on 1 Jan 2019; 297 lines removed (smart watches, some chemicals, child-safety goods) after hearings.
If China retaliates, the President said the Administration will immediately pursue phase three — tariffs on approximately $267 billion of additional imports.
USDA first-wave farm aid $4.7B (of $12B); $3.6B to soybean farmers after China’s soybean tariff. China took $14.2B of US soy in 2016.
Mnuchin had invited Chinese negotiators to resume talks; Beijing said US insistence on tariffs brings new uncertainties. Kudlow: US ready to negotiate anytime if talks are serious.
